source_observations.observation: State or activity of a base. Separately names an own-sense extension, arhat with n and caturveda with two grades.
Yat with deletion of n in stena. Some divide the rule so as also to receive ṣyañ by inheritance.
Plain ya of sakhi and the envoy/trader supplement. The strengthened trade word is referred to brāhmaṇādi.
One suffix on kapi and jñāti, and no ordered pairing of the two bases with the two senses.
Pati-final words and named members with yak. PG736 distinguished the homophonous fire noun.
Living kinds, named ages and the udgātṛ list with a mantra restriction on subhaga.
Aṇ with hāyana-final words and the yuvan class. Additional śrotriya deletion must be marked.
The four classes themselves are the created referent. The passage independently supports the cited own-sense reading.

source_observations.locator: Manu 8.332, Sanskrit and Medhātithi in translation
source_observations.observation: Predicate steyam occurs with bhavet in a contrast between two ways of taking. It attests the unstrengthened word.
Sāyaṇa connects the locative of friendship directly with the grammatical rule, glosses the relation, and specifies affix accent.
The first sakhyam in 5 is governed by jujoṣa; the next has bhavet supplied by Sāyaṇa. In 6 another is governed by pra bravāma.

source_observations.locator: Śākala RV 3.8.2 and 11, text and commentary
source_observations.observation: Two dative singulars in the ritual-post hymn. The modern exposition at 5.1.129 explicitly cites verse 2.
A vocative adjective and neuter plural derivative occur together. The latter is the subject of motion, glossed as possessions.
The first purpose belongs to the taking of the hand. The second dative is the previously owned householder form.
Explains the first dative as for good fortune and the other as for the status of a householder.

source_observations.locator: Gadādhara on Pāraskara Gṛhyasūtra 1.6, end of section
source_observations.observation: Explicit group-of-fortunate-ones analysis before the outer bhāva. Also offers household status or service of the future household fire on the second dative.
The childhood and youth nouns occur in parallel with feminine jarā. Their attachment as stages of the embodied one supports nominatives.
